_doc: Denver Grand Prix (ledger 0096, PLAN.md, DOSSIER.md approved 2026-11-23): a fictional street circuit on Denver's real streets, through Lake Murray v4's engine as Sand Creek is (tracks/sand-creek-lm: engine lm-v4, race and street layouts). The draft line is the lap as OSM's nodes (data/lap_line.plan.json, routed on source/osm.json), rounded, profiled from 3DEP 1 m and widened by source/draft/draft_line.py into the files tools/lm_engine_intake.py reads (lm_intake.source_track is this track). 0.1.0 = Drive 1: the lap's road and ground, the race layout's K-rails, the free roam on the same roads. Every number not measured is marked [invented] in its _doc and listed in ledger 0096 '0.1.0 (Drive 1)'.

fillet._doc: scripts/gps/fillet.py before the 3 m resample. Each of the lap's twelve corners over 45 deg: the circle of radius_m tangent to both legs, radius_m = curb_radius_m + the mean of the two legs' measured half widths (as Sand Creek's route.fillet). curb_radius_m 6.0 is [invented]: no curb return on the lap is measured (source/widths bridges every junction mouth straight across). Every other OSM node is rounded inside its own two segments; simplify_m 0 (merging OSM's near-colinear nodes made the corners' legs long, so a 90 deg corner rounded to a 60 m arc 25 m off the street).

edge._connector_grass_clearance_doc: 0.2.8 (PC, 2026-11-09): the side streets keep 0.2.7's lip (the engine default 0.10, 20 cm under their lane edge); only the mainline's strip is flush. With -0.08 on the connectors too, the rehearsal's audit read I 42 / K 38: where two side streets meet, one street's strip stood 8-22 cm over the other's pavement (e.g. grid_unclassified_9#0#1, grid_primary_7#0), where the lower lip had lain under it. Kevin's ask was the fast curves' edges: the mainline
edge._grass_clearance_doc: 0.2.8 (PC, 2026-11-09; Kevin, asked whether the other circuit tracks have Milford's fast-curve edge mess: "Yes, check them"; Milford 0.1.6 is the same fix, ledger 0087): the strip's outer lip 2 cm under the lane edge (profile point 3 at -grass_clearance = +0.08 over the unlifted edge; the lane edge at +0.10). engine-july's prep holds the ground past the ROAD edge at the lane edge's height - 0.02 for 3 m (its contact band), so the lower lip lay in a gutter with a wall of ground at its lip. Measured on the installed 0.2.7 (gate OBJ, every 10 m, both sides; strip_gutter.py): the strip (1.5 m grade) ends 19 cm under the lane edge; the ground just past it stood more than 5 cm over the lip at 137 of 1,608 side-stations, more than 10 cm at 68 (max 17 cm). Flush with the band, nothing stands over it (none was set: the engine's default 0.10 put the lip 20 cm under the lane edge)
edge._doc: Kevin 2026-11-03 (ledger 0070 Q1): "race curbs, no sidewalks" = race kerbs at the race corners (owed: they come with a race corridor), no street curbs, no sidewalks. The v021 edge strip with no curb: the lane edge stays at road height for 0.30 m, then meets the ground 0.20 m lower over 1.5 m [invented: the shortest run under the drive gate's 0.12 m per 0.5 m]. The strip keeps the assembler's four profile points a side, which tools/weld_mouths_blend.py reads.

declared_medians._doc: Colfax's raised bus-lane median, Sherman to Grant (Kevin 2026-11-27: "raised"; the race keeps "the correct side of the street", the north side): its centre line from the DOTI 100% design, Aug 2024 (section A-A, 24 ft north kerb to median face, 6 ft median) on the measured north kerb (source/colfax_median/colfax_median.py). tools/declared_medians.py writes it as median_bands.json island_w_by_vertex + island_off_by_vertex (the island's centre off the line); the draft's median step authors it (concrete top). Logan to Grant draws no 6 ft median (two abutting bus lanes, a double line) and is not built; Sherman to Lincoln waits for the Colfax curb redo.

widths._doc: the measured kerb-to-kerb edges of source/widths/widths.json (claude/dgp-widths-20261125, 1becc3a0): the kerb face from the 2020 lidar's class-2 step, else the asphalt edge (lidar intensity / 2022 aerial) plus the measured 0.46 m gutter pan, else linear fill. Grades over all 5,318 edges: 73 % measured, 4 % detected, 24 % inferred [invented]: 276 under Stout's roof (linear portal to portal), about 330 at junction mouths (bridged straight across), the rest unread. The line is moved to the middle of its two edges and the width is their distance. Constructions [invented]: offset and width linear across each declared corner (tangent + corner_pad_m 6 m); where Kalamath and Santa Fe share one paved street south of Colfax, each direction's edge is cut at the middle between the two lap lines less divider_clear_m 1.8 m [invented] (the edge strip's own width, so neither ribbon's strip stands on the other's pavement: verify_race O, audit_mesh K): a 3.6 m strip of ground between the two directions where the real street is paved across (paint.json's yellow pieces there read 6.6-6.8 m from Kalamath's line, the middle is about 6.6-7.0 m); running means of 15 m on the offset and 9 m on the width. Where the lap's two directions run within shared_height_m 30 m [invented] of each other (Kalamath / Santa Fe), the two lines' heights are blended to their mean (full weight within 20 m): one street, one deck height, so the ground between the two ribbons never stands over the lower one; the real crossfall is not measured.

edge_fills.why: [invented] 15th St short of Lawrence (widths frame s 2,287.5-2,325; OSM s 2,284-2,316): the 5 m pit in 3DEP's ground (DOSSIER 3, read as an artefact; this config's 15th St straight span) is in the lidar's class-2 returns too, and the kerb reader found steps inside it: 5.75-11 m kerb to kerb where the street either side reads 16-21 m. Both edges filled linearly between the measured stations at its ends; drive_test street read grass on top in the lane at the pinch (r6)

Colfax, Grant to Sherman (the raised bus-lane median's block; the Colfax curb redo 2026-11-27): the 2020 lidar's south 'kerb' at s 6,622.5 and 6,625 (-4.38 / -4.34 m N) is the north face of a raised refuge island the same survey lists there (widths.json medians: left 6.25-7.62 m), not the kerb, which reads -15.17 / -14.80 at the two stations either side. Through the draft's running means and Lake Murray's line smoothing it stood the built NORTH edge 0.9-1.3 m inside the measured north kerb at v40-44. Filled linearly between s 6,620 and 6,627.5: the south edge goes to its kerb, the north edge's readings there (5.12 / 5.41) are within 0.04 m of the fill. The 2024 design (DOTI 100%, section A-A) draws no island there: Kevin's newest source per feature

mouths._doc: source/draft/mouth_stubs.py: each side street's mouth for the free roam (the brief's 0.1.0 street layout: the lap's own roads plus each side street's mouth; the full D4 grid comes later). OSM ways meeting the lap's own nodes, followed along OSM's line for reach_m 40 m [invented]; parallel_m 20 m [invented] (a stub whose far end stays this close to the lap is the lap's other carriageway); min_m 12 m [invented] of it off the lap's pavement; widths by class [invented] (Sand Creek's grid table, links 6 m): the side streets' kerbs are not measured. Service roads (alleys, drives) are not mouths here. keep_both_on_lap false: a piece that meets the lap again within its reach (Colfax between Speer's two legs, the Speer / Stout / Kalamath junction) is not built in 0.1.0: its two welded ends failed verify_mouths (notch, approach) in the first run other_lap_clear_m 6 m [invented]: a stub stops before it reaches another part of the lap (Colfax between Speer's two legs, the Speer / Stout / Kalamath junction).
mouths._exclude_doc: mouths not built in 0.1.0, each with the gate reading that refused it on the Mac (r8): the junction machinery (mouth returns, pads) Sand Creek uses at its hard junctions is owed for these; the street there is the lap's edge, as everywhere a mouth is not built

layouts.name: Race
layouts.run: the lap, one way, as every street on it runs (PLAN 2: 0 m against traffic): Colfax west from the Capitol, Speer, Stout under the Convention Center, 15th, Blake over Cherry Creek, Speer, Kalamath south across Colfax, W 14th Ave, Santa Fe and the northbound Kalamath back to Speer, W 14th Ave over the creek, 14th Ave up Capitol Hill, Logan, Colfax to the line
layouts.ui_description: Denver Grand Prix: a fictional street circuit on Denver's real streets, 6.5 km one way from the Colorado State Capitol, the streets as the 2022 aerial and the 2020 lidar measured them: concrete barriers along both edges, the side streets sealed. Drive 1: the road and the ground; the city, its lamps, signals, signs and paint come later. The AI line is a generated draft, not an in-game recording.
layouts._start_doc: the line at the Colfax / Sherman crosswalk (vertex 50 of the finished line, 152 m after station 0), the grid behind it on Colfax facing west, in the north lane beside the bus-lane median (Kevin 2026-11-27: "the correct side of the street"): columns at 6.03 / 8.03 m right of the centre line, the one offset (7.00-7.05 m) at which the spawn gate holds both columns 0.3 m clear of the closure and the north K-rail at every vertex from the pole back past the last slot [invented: 7.03 inside it]; the pits single file at their own offset (Kevin: "Yes, both"), 4.33 m right, the middle of the 3.88-4.78 m where all eight clear 0.3 m on the narrower street toward Grant

layouts.ui_description: Denver Grand Prix Free Roam: the Denver Grand Prix lap's streets open, as the 2022 aerial and the 2020 lidar measured them. Drive 1: the lap's own roads; the side streets and the city grid come later.
layouts._start_doc: the free roam's grid as the race's (columns 6.03 / 8.03 m right of the centre line, north of the bus-lane median; verify_kn5 holds street spawns right of travel) and its pits at 4.33 m right, as the race's; the line at the Sherman crosswalk

race._doc: Lake Murray's race furniture as Sand Creek's race layout uses it (ledger 0079 round K; tools/barrier_bands.py, tools/author_race_furniture_blend.py, the race gates): Kevin's 4.04 m K-rail module swept along both edges of the whole lap, 0.82 m in from the lane edge (road mode), sealing every side street; the race kerbs at the corners the detector finds (race kn5 only). The free roam loads none of it.
race._spawn_gate_layouts_doc: ledger 0079 round K: the spawn self-gate holds the race layout's grid clear of the strips; the free roam loads no strip and keeps its grid in the right-hand lane

corridor._doc: the race is the WHOLE street, one way, the entire lap (as Sand Creek round K): no boxes, no closure runs; the K-rails along both measured edges seal every mouth. clear_width_m and the solver knobs are Lake Murray's (ledger 0049), read only by closure runs, of which there are none.

noses.why: Colfax's raised bus-lane median, Sherman to Grant (Kevin 2026-11-27: "raised", the race on "the correct side of the street"): its east nose; the K-rail across the south carriageway beside it seals the far side
the same median's west nose, short of the Sherman crosswalk and the start line (v50)

hard_min_zones.why: Kevin, 2026-11-27, from his Apple TV, verbatim: "allow it narrow there". He was answering: "The city drew Colfax's raised median only from Sherman to Grant (56 m, the start/finish block). With a barrier lining it, the race lane there is 5.4-7.0 m between barriers, under Denver's 6.5 m minimum (an invented number borrowed from Lake Murray). Allow it narrower there (5.3 m minimum, that block only), or paint the median flat?" The median run v28-v45 and its two nose pins only; 6.5 m everywhere else

radius_zones.why: Kevin, 2026-11-27, in chat, verbatim: "Yes, both". He was answering: "Allow the 14.4 m bend at Grant and move the pits closer to the line?" The closure along Colfax's median at its Grant nose (pin v27, the island's 9 m nose taper to v31) follows the taper on that narrow street; 20 m everywhere else. Codex was asked (claude-resume.to_codex_colfax_median_nose) to make the barrier follow the real nose, which may retire this

corridor._closure_doc: the north lane sealed along the median by the fleet's usual K-rail (closure run v27-v46, island_mode pavement), the south carriageway beside it closed at both noses; whole street everywhere else (as Sand Creek round K before the median)
